name: Metaxism
summary: Metaxism is the authoritarian, ultra-nationalist and monarchist outlook of Ioannis Metaxas and his 4th of August Regime in Greece (1936-1941). It rejected parliamentary democracy, liberalism and communism, sought a disciplined 'New State' under a Leader and king, and aimed at national regeneration as a 'Third Hellenic Civilisation' joining ancient Greek and Byzantine Orthodox legacies. Scholars debate whether it was conservative-authoritarian or a partial fascism.
scope: The ideology and practice of the Metaxas dictatorship (1936-1941), based on Metaxas's 4 August 1936 proclamation, his speeches as quoted by Kallis, and the regime's ideologues Mantzoufas and Koumaros; it excludes later claimants such as the 1967 junta and Golden Dawn. Economic, gender and many modern questions are inferred, since the regime had no systematic programme.

sources.usedFor: Corporatism, labour and strikes, welfare, repression, minorities, women in EON, economy.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: The regime set minimum wages and promised material improvement for workers and farmers, but a substantial rise was not an explicit goal.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Metaxas aimed to replace capitalism with a corporatist order and directed public works, so he trusted the state over free markets; he still kept private property.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The proclamation speaks of helping the poorer classes but nothing is documented on wealth taxation; the order was cross-class and paternalist.

unions-good.rationale: Strikes were banned and unions were put under state control via the Workers' Centre, since the regime tied labour unrest to communism.

property-fundamental.rationale: Private property was kept against communism, but the nation and state were placed above individual rights, so it is not treated as nearly inviolable.

cut-welfare.rationale: The regime introduced unemployment insurance, maternity leave and IKA, and promoted improvement for the poorer classes, so it did not see welfare as harmful.

worker-ownership.rationale: Corporatism sought class cooperation under state direction rather than worker ownership, which is a socialist idea the regime opposed.

strong-leader.rationale: Metaxas took all power, was called Archigos (Leader), and demanded full discipline to the state.

state-harmful.rationale: The ideology is statist: the nation and state are transcendent and demand full discipline.

empower-police-military.rationale: Martial law, mass arrests of about 15,000 and exile of dissidents show a regime built on police and military authority.

decide-locally.rationale: A centralised state demanding full discipline and a totalitarian national project leaves little room for local decision-making.

traditional-family.rationale: The regime's values were Country, Loyalty, Family and Religion, and EON trained girls as wives and mothers.

more-religion-public.rationale: Orthodoxy was a core pillar of the Third Hellenic Civilisation and the church was given a larger role in education and moral guidance.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The proclamation calls for keeping national traditions and Greek culture, and the whole project is cultural regeneration.

gradual-change.rationale: It was a radical national rebirth imposed from above, yet in a conservative framing; it overturned institutions rather than respecting them.

free-trade.rationale: The regime sought a self-directed corporatist economy and public works; protectionism is listed with the ideology but not detailed in sources.

nation-first.rationale: Individual interests were subordinate to the nation and national regeneration was the supreme goal; neutrality was pursued for national interest.

open-borders.rationale: Ethnic-Orthodox national identity with exclusion of minorities is incompatible with open borders.

revolution-justified.rationale: Metaxas called his 1936 takeover a national regeneration against a communist revolution; he justified a coup from above but opposed revolution from below.

experts-over-public.rationale: Metaxas presented the government as above party and parliament and ruled by decree, implying rule by those with the right national vision over the public.

central-planning.rationale: The regime directed investment and public works and planned corporatism, but not a fully planned economy.

socialized-markets.rationale: Corporatism combined private property with state control, not worker or public ownership under markets.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Protectionism is associated with the regime in the sources' lists, though not elaborated.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The regime funded public works, stabilised the drachma and set price floors, steering the economy toward national goals.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: The ideology was founded in opposition to communism and socialism.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: The regime stabilised the drachma through the state; abolition is contrary to its statism.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: The regime aimed to replace capitalism with a corporatist system organised by branches of production, with compulsory arbitration of labour disputes.

one-party-rule.rationale: Metaxas abolished all parties including his own and ruled through the state and EON, not a ruling party; some tendencies toward a state ideology.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about a monarch who rules, and the statement now asks only about a ceremonial head of state, on which the sources cited here are silent.

reviewHistory.rationale: Metaxas was a staunch royalist and the regime rested on King George II and the monarchy as national continuity.
reviewHistory.author: claude-sonnet-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about a monarch who rules, and the statement now asks only about a ceremonial head of state, on which the sources cited here are silent.

democracy-best.rationale: Metaxas openly condemned parliamentary democracy and called democracy a failure.

direct-votes.rationale: Parliamentary politics was abolished and no popular votes were held; he rejected popular party politics entirely.

workers-councils.rationale: A communist-style council system is the opposite of the regime's anti-communist authoritarianism.

right-to-secede.rationale: An ultra-nationalist unitary state repressed Slavic regionalism and irredentists.

political-violence-never.rationale: Metaxas promised to exterminate opposition in the harshest way and the regime used arrest and torture.

war-builds-character.rationale: It held up the militarist societies of Macedonia and Sparta as part of the Greek civilisational model and urged Spartan self-control on Greeks.

separate-church-state.rationale: The regime kept state control over the church and fused religion with national identity, even appointing a new Holy Synod.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Orthodoxy was invoked as a pillar of the 'Third Hellenic Civilisation', but law was made by decree of Metaxas and the king, and Kallis notes no clerical rule; religion legitimised the state rather than supplying its laws.

private-courts-defense.rationale: A centralised state demanding full discipline excludes private provision of law and force.

military-superiority.rationale: Metaxas was a general who admired military discipline and Megali Idea, though foreign policy was cautious and neutral.

ethnic-nation.rationale: True Greeks were defined as ethnically Greek and Orthodox, with Albanians, Slavs and Turks meant to be excluded.

class-struggle-history.rationale: It rejected the Marxist reading and promoted national unity above classes.

equal-outcomes.rationale: The regime sought welfare and improvement for the poorer classes but a national hierarchy, not equality of outcomes.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not applicable; the regime's minority policy was assimilationist toward Slavs.

civilizational-union.rationale: It emphasised a Greek-specific civilisation, not union with other Orthodox or Mediterranean peoples.

self-interest-moral.rationale: The EON oath called for virtuous non-individualistic citizens and individual interests were subordinated to the nation.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Freedom was tied to discipline of the state, and duty to nation outranked individuals.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The regime built roads, railways, airports and industry; it saw modernisation partly as corrupting yet pursued public works.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Its programme was reactionary and rooted in tradition, not disruptive acceleration.

restore-past-order.rationale: It was palingenetic, reviving ancient and Byzantine legacies, yet framed as creating a new Greece, so tradition and renewal mix.

results-over-ideology.rationale: The regime had an explicit ideology (Third Hellenic Civilisation) and held that national regeneration comes first.

direct-action.rationale: It took power by a coup from above and ruled outside elections, but direct action by the masses was not its way.

means-match-ends.rationale: It used harsh repression in service of national regeneration; means were not meant to mirror ends.

return-to-foraging.rationale: The ideology idealised the high civilisations of Sparta and Byzantium and built modern infrastructure.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Corporatism organises production by branches and classes cooperate; it rejects communism.

distribute-by-need.rationale: A communist distribution principle opposed by the regime, though it offered welfare to the poor.

production-for-use.rationale: The regime kept private enterprise within a corporatist framework; not framed this way.

profit-exploitation.rationale: It rejected Marxist analysis of class exploitation and promoted employer-worker partnership.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Metaxas's regime existed to prevent communist revolution.

collective-farming.rationale: It opposed communism and gave debt relief and price floors to individual farmers.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist thesis rejected by an anti-communist nationalist regime.

taxation-theft.rationale: A statist regime financing public works and welfare rejects this libertarian claim.

harm-principle.rationale: The state could suppress any opposition and censor books and music for national morals.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Individuals were subordinated to the nation and civil rights were suspended.

exit-over-voice.rationale: It demanded full discipline to the state and denied that either exit or voting limits authority.

state-as-business.rationale: The state was a sacred national entity, not a service provider to customers.

positive-liberty.rationale: The regime paired freedom with state discipline and provided welfare, but did not frame freedom as material means.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Metaxist nationalism stressed ethnos and culture, and the regime was not antisemitic; no racial-science doctrine documented.

organic-representation.rationale: Corporatism and organic national thinking, with parties abolished, suit representation through occupational bodies, though never built.

total-state.rationale: Metaxas called his regime totalitarian and aimed to direct education, culture, youth and economy.

national-rebirth.rationale: The Third Hellenic Civilisation was a palingenetic project of national rebirth against decadence.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Metaxas kept Greece neutral and defensive until the Italian invasion of 1940 and did not revive the Megali Idea's claims on Asia Minor, though the regime's rhetoric looked back to Hellenic greatness.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Loyalty to the king and Leader was central, but this is a feudal model unlike a modern state with EON oath and decrees.

bound-labor.rationale: Corporatism and welfare, with debt relief for farmers; no feudal bondage.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: It censored thought for national ends, but held to eternal national and religious truths rather than relativism.

universal-morality.rationale: Orthodoxy was held as an eternal moral core for the nation; universalism across cultures was not stressed.

single-common-good.rationale: It presented government as above party and class, aiming at one national good, not interest balancing.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: The regime was tolerant toward Jews but did not address Zionism; no stance documented.

revive-national-language.rationale: The regime promoted a conservative Demotic in schools, not revival of a lost language.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Strikes banned and labour put under state control; no democratic voice in firms.

school-vouchers.rationale: EON and state education were to shape youth; private school choice was not favoured.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: The regime funded public works yet stabilised the drachma; no stated doctrine.

economic-freedom.rationale: Political freedom was to be subordinated to state discipline and the economy was to be steered by corporatism.

rule-by-example.rationale: The Leader cult stressed moral example but the regime relied on censorship and repression too.

national-self-determination.rationale: It insists on Greek national sovereignty but denied minorities within Greece the same.

force-without-un.rationale: The UN did not exist; the regime avoided war until attacked.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Orthodox faith and national myth were central; reason alone was not the guide.

class-collaboration.rationale: Corporatism and EON aimed to unite classes under the nation and rejected class struggle.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: It stressed preserving the Hellenic legacy and revival of historic civilisation.

workers-nation.rationale: It organised workers along national lines and opposed international communism.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Its nationalism was ethnic-Orthodox, but the regime was not antisemitic, banned antisemitic newspaper publications, and set up no racial classification in law.

state-class-instrument.rationale: It rejects the Marxist view and sees the state as a sacred national entity above classes.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Slavic cultural expression was repressed and minorities were pressed toward Greek culture.

elite-replacement.rationale: Not a Metaxist theme; the regime was not antisemitic and no replacement theory existed.

proportional-representation.rationale: Elections and parliament were abolished with parties.

national-mission.rationale: The Third Hellenic Civilisation was to elevate Greeks and eventually world civilisation, a mission that is cultural more than a drive to export a regime.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: The proclamation blames parliament and party conflicts, and Metaxas stressed the parliamentary elite's squabbles and failure.

night-watchman-state.rationale: A totalitarian state directing every sphere is the opposite.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Its identity was ethno-religious Greek, but no racial purity doctrine is documented and it was tolerant of Jews.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: It was tolerant toward Jews and Muslims but defined true Greeks by ethnicity and religion.

socialism-one-country.rationale: It opposed socialism entirely; the thesis is a communist one.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Orthodox religion was central to education and citizenship formation.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: The regime strengthened the state but not on socialist grounds; it only matches in the abstract.

consent-of-governed.rationale: It dissolved parliament and held no elections; legitimacy came from the king and Leader.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The regime used force against opponents and promised to exterminate opposition.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: It held class and individual competition to be corrosive, preferring organic unity and discipline.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: It abolished all parties and banned the communists, justified by the communist threat.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: It held freedom as discipline to the state, with arbitrary power in the Leader.

separated-powers.rationale: Power was concentrated in Metaxas and parliament was dissolved.

vanguard-party.rationale: A communist doctrine opposed by the regime.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The proclamation promised the poorer classes help and social insurance was introduced, though not as a first priority.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: The regime founded workers' housing; but no policy documented.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Strikes were banned outright and labour disputes sent to arbitration.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Its ethno-Orthodox nationalism held that national unity requires a shared ethnicity and religion.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: It rejected even elections; lotteries are contrary to rule by the Leader.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Metaxas declared martial law and suspended civil rights against communism.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: The regime set price floors on some farm goods and fought economic crisis through the state.

party-controls-media.rationale: The 4th of August regime imposed press censorship and ran state propaganda through Kotzias's and Nikoloudis's ministry; the statement allows control by the government, which is what the regime practised, even without a ruling party.

party-commands-army.rationale: The army remained under the king and state; parties were abolished.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: EON stressed discipline, but parties were abolished, so applicability is limited.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: It was ultra-nationalist and totalitarian with nation above all.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The king and Metaxas held command; the regime favoured executive power over the legislature.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Orthodoxy is governed by bishops and Metaxas dissolved the Holy Synod to install a loyal one.

clerical-rule.rationale: Kallis finds no clerical fascism; religion legitimised but did not rule.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: A Leninist idea contrary to the regime's nationalism and anti-communism.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: It banned Marx, Freud, Tolstoy and Kant and repressed rebetiko music for national morals.

recall-officials.rationale: Citizens had no power over the Leader.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Workers' housing was built but no abolition; unconnected to the regime.

people-in-arms.rationale: A professional army under the king was the backbone of the regime.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Megali Idea irredentism was part of the Third Hellenic Civilisation myth.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Metaxas was a general distrustful of liberal intellectuals but also banned books to guide education.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: It held the Greek civilisation as a superior historic heritage.

restrict-pornography.rationale: A censorious regime defending national morals would restrict it.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: True Greeks were defined by ethnicity and Orthodoxy.

minority-language-support.rationale: The 4th of August Regime article states that it continued repressing the use of Slavic languages in public and in private and persecuted Slavic-speakers in Macedonia.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: EON and censorship sought uniform virtuous citizens.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: The regime stabilised the drachma and gave debt relief to farmers, but this was domestic.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Not a concern for this ideology.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Metaxas planned a new constitution by himself, not an assembly.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The head of state was a hereditary king.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Individual interests were subordinate to the nation and corporatist.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Metaxas viewed the Soviet Union as another totalitarian regime and rejected socialism; the state-capitalist theory itself isn't from him.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The king was above party, but also an active partner in the dictatorship.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: It repressed Slavic regionalists and maintained a unitary nationalist state.

region-keeps-system.rationale: It denied autonomy to minorities and centralised the state.

character-from-environment.rationale: EON aimed to shape the new man by education, implying environment forms character.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Metaxas ruled by decree above the constitution but invoked a constitutional order.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Neither mixed nor balanced; concentrated authority was favoured.

leader-cult.rationale: Metaxas was called the Archigos and made an effort at a personal cult.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist or Maoist thesis opposed by the regime.

land-redistribution.rationale: Farmers received debt relief rather than land redistribution.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: The Megali Idea envisioned a Greek realm over areas where Greeks lived.

common-currency.rationale: The regime stabilised the national drachma; nationalist in outlook.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Greek uniqueness was stressed; no pan-Balkan union.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: It excluded minorities from citizenship and repressed Slavic expression.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: It rejected Marxism and rested on spiritual and national myths.

ban-cartels.rationale: Corporatism organises industry by branches, not competition law.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: It rejected both majorities and constitutional constraints.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Public roles by gender in EON were distinct; the regime offered no gender parity.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Protectionism is associated with it, yet Greece traded; Britain and Germany were trade partners.

moral-incentives.rationale: It stressed national duty and discipline over individualism, though wages stayed.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: It preferred coup from above by army and king.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Third Hellenic Civilisation centred schooling on Greek ancient and Byzantine heritage.

patriotic-education.rationale: EON oath and compulsory membership taught national pride and loyalty.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The regime sought to replace capitalism with corporatism yet fought communism; no stated view on collapse.

former-empire-influence.rationale: The Megali Idea sought Byzantine legacy influence.

delink-world-market.rationale: Greece was trading with Britain and Germany.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: A statist regime regulating all spheres would not leave associational freedom wholly to owners.

elective-rulers.rationale: It was a monarchy led by an appointed Prime Minister.

minority-veto.rationale: Discipline and unity required that dissent not bind.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The proclamation blames parliament's incapacity; Metaxas suspended parliament on 4 August 1936 and ruled as royal prime minister without it.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Paternalism: the regime promised help for the poor from above.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: EON demanded active participation in the national project.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Not a Metaxist statement; it ruled by repression and propaganda.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Dependency theory is Marxist-linked and not part of the regime's thinking.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Greece had no settler-indigenous divide, and the question does not map onto Metaxist nationalism, which defined Greeks by ethnicity and Orthodoxy.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Metaxas aligned with other totalitarian regimes against democracy.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Metaxas himself called the Soviet Union totalitarian alongside Germany and Italy, but he did not condemn them equally.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: It valued historical heritage and tradition.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: It stressed a Greek-specific model against liberal-democratic models.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Metaxas, from the army tradition, believed in the army as guarantor of stability.

paid-care-work.rationale: Mothers' roles were domestic, though maternity leave existed.

filial-duty.rationale: Family values and loyalty were central; filial piety not specifically stated.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Not compatible with the Leader's rule.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: The regime created state social insurance (IKA).

land-use-tenure.rationale: Individual farmers had debt relief; no communal land.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Parliament was dissolved and rule was by decree.

single-official-language.rationale: The regime defined Greekness by Greek language and Orthodoxy and forced minority languages, notably Slavic speech in Macedonia, out of public life.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: An authoritarian ethnic nationalism that defined the nation by descent and religion and had no concept of outcome-based anti-discrimination. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

democratic-peace.rationale: The regime rejected parliamentary democracy and liberalism, so spreading democracy was no aim.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: A disciplined authoritarian state demanded obedience to the Leader and the law.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The regime's nationalism was not built on a minority-conspiracy myth; Kallis treats it as differing from fascism here.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: It exalted Orthodox family and morality as pillars of the Third Hellenic Civilisation.

public-access-to-information.rationale: An authoritarian regime that censored the press and ruled by decree did not open government to the public.

informal-organisation.rationale: It banned parties and organised youth and labour through the state, rejecting independent small groups.

religious-nation.rationale: The regime defined the nation through Orthodox Christianity as part of the 'Helleno-Christian' civilisation.

defeat-communism.rationale: The regime banned the KKE, jailed communists and defined itself against communism as a core purpose.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Metaxas explicitly rejected both parliamentary capitalism and communism in favour of a 'Third Hellenic Civilisation' and New State.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The 4 August proclamation suspended parliament and key constitutional rights, banned parties and political activity, and targeted communists as a threat to order.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Kallis shows the regime made Orthodoxy a pillar of the nation and restricted other faiths and proselytism.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The regime abolished parliamentary politics for a disciplined, top-down New State under a Leader.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: The regime held that the nation, not class or other groups, was the unit of politics, and rejected the class struggle as divisive. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The regime was a military-backed nationalist dictatorship that prized the army and prepared for defence.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The regime suspended parliament and the constitution in 1936 and ruled by decree and emergency law, and the Leader's will stood above legal constraint.

racial-franchise.rationale: The regime's nationalism was Hellenic, but it did not restrict the franchise by ethnicity; the 1936 proclamation targets parliament and communism, not an ethnic vote rule.

citizens-assembly.rationale: The regime abolished parliament and rested on a Leader and king; the 1936 proclamation rejects parliamentary politics, so decisions by lot-chosen citizens would be alien to it. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Metaxas denounced plutocracy rhetorically but defended private property under a corporatist order, so adherents split; not a stated programme.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The Third Hellenic Civilisation fused Hellenism with Orthodoxy and the regime promoted Christian education, so an atheist state is the opposite of its aims.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: The New State relied on police, censorship and internal exile to enforce order and fight communism; abolition is contrary to it.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The regime built paternalist state welfare but also stressed the Church and charity; no stated view on the balance.

vote-delegation.rationale: The proclamation ended parliamentary democracy and party politics, so citizen vote delegation is excluded. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

uniformed-youth.rationale: The regime built the National Youth Organisation (EON), a uniformed, drilled movement meant to train youth in national and Orthodox values.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Its anti-plutocratic, corporatist rhetoric put labour and the national community above pure capital, though it never stated this as a principle.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: A regime built on military virtue and national struggle would hold that killing in defence of self or nation is justified.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: The 'Third Hellenic Civilisation' explicitly joined ancient Greece and Byzantium to the present as one continuous national story.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Metaxist ideals of the family and nation assumed a fixed natural category of women, as an inference from its traditionalism.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: The regime's cult of national sacrifice and Orthodox heroism honoured those who died for Greece in near-sacred terms.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: The regime framed its project as a spiritual regeneration of Greece through Orthodox Christianity against materialism and communism.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: The regime rejected communism and class politics.

person-over-state.rationale: The regime placed the nation and state above the individual, rejecting liberalism.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Metaxism's Third Hellenic Civilisation joined ancient Greek and Byzantine Orthodox legacies, making religion part of national life.

communal-electorates.rationale: Metaxas rejected parliamentary politics and party divisions in favour of one organic nation under a Leader, so separate religious electorates contradict it.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Metaxas's militarist nationalism demanded discipline and duty to the nation, and refusal of orders would be treason.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Metaxas ended the parliamentary system by coup and built a New State on its ruins; the statement is read as replacing the old order.

sacred-nation.rationale: Metaxas's Third Hellenic Civilisation makes the nation an eternal community joining ancient Greek and Byzantine heritage, with the nation above the individual.

public-service-media.rationale: The regime censored the press and ran state propaganda and a single youth organisation; media free of government control was refused. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

religions-one-truth.rationale: The regime made Greek Orthodoxy the core of the Third Hellenic Civilisation and its national identity, which rules out all religions being one truth.

workers-own-party.rationale: The regime banned parties and strikes and replaced class conflict with corporatism under the Leader, so an independent workers' party was rejected.

one-language-many-names.rationale: The regime defined Greekness ethnically and suppressed Slavic-language use in the north, so one Greek language was the line.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: The regime made Orthodoxy the heart of the Third Hellenic Civilisation and favoured it over other faiths.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: The proclamation rejects parliamentary party competition as destructive and sets up a Leader-led state without free elections. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

women-suffrage.rationale: The regime abolished parliament, so there was no vote for anyone; it did not extend rights and viewed women through the family and EON.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: The regime built national life on Orthodoxy and the family, so it saw religion as supporting women's role.

homestead-ownership.rationale: The regime had no theory of first appropriation; its corporatist economy gave the state a large role, so the answer is neutral.

national-church-status.rationale: The regime made the Greek Orthodox Church the national church and part of its idea of Hellenic civilisation, with strong church-state ties.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Metaxism defined Greekness ethnically and suppressed minorities, such as Slavic speakers, so territorial autonomy was rejected.

simple-living.rationale: The regime praised rural and Orthodox virtues but also pursued industrial and military build-up, so the answer is neutral.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: The Third Hellenic Civilisation fused ancient Greece and Orthodox Byzantium into a sacred national heritage the regime vowed to defend.

self-ownership.rationale: The New State subordinated the individual to the nation and state, with compulsory youth membership and censorship.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: The regime abolished parties and parliament and made the Leader the focus of national unity, though it kept corporatist bodies and its own youth organisation.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Greek Orthodoxy was a pillar of the Third Hellenic Civilisation and the regime closely tied church and state, defining the nation by religion.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: The Third Hellenic Civilisation sought modern, disciplined national renewal grounded in ancient and Byzantine heritage, joining modernity to ancestral values.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: The regime did not address international finance taxes; its corporatist and autarkic leanings point both ways.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: The regime's suspension of the constitution and rule by the Leader's decree place the state's law above individual conscience.

multipolar-world.rationale: Metaxas sought to keep Greece neutral between powers while relying on Britain, but did not state a world-order view.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: The regime rejected Marxism and class struggle, so Marx's labour theory of value would be rejected.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: The regime claimed to unite nation and workers through class collaboration and built social insurance, but not in the left's solidarity sense.

missingStatements.text: All young people should be required to belong to a single state youth organisation that trains them in discipline and loyalty to the nation.
missingStatements.rationale: Metaxas founded EON as the only youth organisation, with compulsory membership and abolition of rivals, as his main tool for creating a new generation.

notes: Scholars split between conservative authoritarian (Payne, Fleischer) and quasi- or para-fascist readings (Kallis, Kofas), so totalitarian answers are strongest where Metaxas himself used the word. Economic and social questions are mostly inferred, so many answers are low confidence.
